prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode transport rejects requests whose Accept header lists only `application/json`, because the handler enforces that Accept include BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream` even when the server is configured for JSON-only response mode. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode transport rejects requests whose Accept header lists only `application/json`, because the handler enforces that Accept include BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream` even when the server is configured for JSON-only response mode. Both PRs patch the exact same Accept-header validation block in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts to relax that requirement. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that follows RFC 7231 Accept-header semantics: it splits on commas, strips whitespace/case, parses media-type parameters, excludes entries with q=0, and matches type/subtype (including wildcard ranges). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which doesn't honor q=0 exclusion or wildcard media ranges (e.g. `application/*`, `*/*`) and is more prone to false positives/negatives on multi-value or parameterized Accept headers. #1996's approach handles a strictly wider and more correct set of Accept-header cases for the same fix.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that follows RFC 7231 Accept-header semantics: it splits on commas, strips whitespace/case, parses media-type parameters, excludes entries with q=0, and matches type/subtype (including wildcard ranges). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which doesn't honor q=0 exclusion or wildcard media ranges (e.g. `application/*`, `*/*`) and is more prone to false positives/negatives on multi-value or parameterized Accept headers. #1996's approach handles a strictly wider and more correct set of Accept-header cases for the same fix.

members.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
members.author: Genmin
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode transport rejects requests whose Accept header lists only `application/json`, because the handler enforces that Accept include BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream` even when the server is configured for JSON-only response mode. Both PRs patch the exact same Accept-header validation block in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts to relax that requirement. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 2215 includes the same trailing-slash normalization as 2214 (via a new normalizeDiscoveryPath helper) but also updates shouldAttemptFallback's root-path check from pathname === '/' to pathname === '' to match the newly-normalized empty-string root value. Applying 2214 alone would silently break that existing check (root path would no longer equal '/' after stripping), causing unnecessary fallback discovery requests at the root path. 2215 is the superset fix that keeps the two pieces of logic consistent; 2214 only has half the fix.
